Research supports evaluating evidence grounding separately from recommendation accuracy: fluent explanations can contain unsupported claims, while explanation effectiveness and user satisfaction measure different outcomes ([factual-consistency study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24366), [explanation evaluation](https://research-portal.uu.nl/en/publications/evaluating-the-effectiveness-of-explanations-for-recommender-syst/)). An adapted annotation protocol should use one recommendation–history–feedback case per unit, recording evidence spans from available titles, descriptions, timestamps and explicit feedback. Label each failure type supported, contradicted or unknown. Functional overlap requires documented shared function; calling it unwanted redundancy requires explicit feedback. Compatibility requires explicit specifications; absent evidence means unknown, not incompatible. Old interactions alone cannot establish stale intent. Unassessable identity remains unknown. Never infer ownership, unmet need or simulator traits. These are proposed operational labels, not a validated taxonomy.

Pilot a written codebook with independent annotators, measure agreement before adjudication, and report per-label Krippendorff’s alpha alongside raw agreement, prevalence, unknown rates and uncertainty; sparse labels can make reliability estimates uninformative ([Krippendorff](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/19312458.2011.568376)). Validate automated diagnostic labels against independently annotated cases, preserving unknown as an explicit outcome. Calibrate diagnostic abstention thresholds on a separate annotation subset, then evaluate on untouched annotated cases: coverage is the fraction receiving a substantive label; selective risk is the error rate among accepted labels. Report risk–coverage curves, per-category results and confidence intervals; confidence scores alone do not establish risk control ([selective classification](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2017/hash/4a8423d5e91fda00bb7e46540e2b0cf1-Abstract.html)). Keep this diagnostic validation separate from unchanged host macro HR@10; diagnostic abstention must not remove benchmark users or candidates.
